title: How to evaluate a model for your use case: Emmanuel Turlay
talk_summary: Emmanuel Turlay argues generic benchmarks (BLEU, ROUGE, GLUE, HellaSwag, TriviaQA, ARC) don't predict performance on your specific task, so each application needs its own eval set. His 'magic trick' is LLM-as-judge: feed your eval dataset through the candidate model, then score outputs with a grading prompt describing the task and a numerical scale, and compare score distributions across models.

takeaways.technique: LLM-as-judge scoring prompt over a task-specific eval set
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a fixed eval dataset through each candidate model, then pass each output into a grading prompt that states the task, the properties to grade, and a 1-10 scale, and have a scoring model emit a number; aggregate into a score distribution per model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can describe to nlm what you're trying to accomplish and what are the grading criteria and ask it to grade the out of another llm on a numerical scale

takeaways.technique: Cheapest-capable selection backed by per-task eval scores
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than trusting leaderboards, they measure each model on the actual input distribution of the application and choose based on that evidence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these metrics will not tell you how each model performs so each application needs to come up with its own evaluation procedure

takeaways.technique: Cheap judge model instead of GPT-4 for bulk scoring
takeaways.what_they_do: They note GPT-4 is the best grader but costly at scale, and use Flan-T5 as a speed/correctness tradeoff for scoring large datasets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have found that flan C5 offers a good trade-off of speed and correctness

takeaways.technique: Distribution of scores, not a single pass/fail
takeaways.what_they_do: They score every item in the eval set and compare the resulting distribution across models rather than relying on one aggregate number.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can draw a distribution of that particular metric

takeaways.technique: Treat evals as a CI test suite
takeaways.what_they_do: They frame model evaluation as analogous to running a test suite in the CI pipeline, run on a held-out dataset independent of training data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can compare evaluation to running a test Suite in your continuous integration pipeline
